# Master paradigms and grammatical terms

### A.1 The two pronoun sets

**Set B (absolutive).** Marks the subject of an intransitive verb, the object of a transitive verb, and the subject of a non-verbal predicate (noun, adjective, positional, k'o).

| Person | Before a consonant (on verbs) | Before a vowel (on verbs) | Free word with non-verbal predicates | Independent pronoun |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1s | i- | in- | in | rin |
| 2s | a- | at- | at | rat |
| 3s | Ø | Ø | Ø | rija' |
| 1p | oj- | oj- | öj | röj |
| 2p | ix- | ix- | ïx | rix |
| 3p | e- | e'- | e | rije' |

Examples: yib'e "I go", yinel "I leave", in tijonel "I am a teacher", öj k'o "we are here", e nima'q "they are big".

**Set A (ergative).** Marks the subject of a transitive verb and the possessor of a noun.

| Person | On nouns, before a consonant | On nouns, before a vowel | On verbs, before a consonant | On verbs, before a vowel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1s | nu- | w- | in- | inw- |
| 2s | a- | aw- | a- | aw- |
| 3s | ru- | r- | ru- (u- after x-, n-, xt-, t-) | r- |
| 1p | qa- | q- | qa- | q- |
| 2p | i- | iw- | i- | iw- |
| 3p | ki- | k- | ki- | k- |

Examples: nutz'i' "my dog", wochoch "my house", ninb'än "I do it", xinlöq' "I bought it", ninwajo' "I want it", xutij "he ate it", xrak'axaj "she heard it", nrajo' "she wants it", kochoch "their house".

### A.2 Aspect and mood prefixes

| Label | Before zero 3sB | Elsewhere | Example with -b'e "go" |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incompletive (present) | n- | y- | nb'e "she goes", yib'e "I go" |
| Completive (past) | x- | x- | xb'e, xib'e |
| Potential (future) | xt- | xk- | xtib'e, xkib'e |
| Imperative / hortative | t- | k- | tib'e "let him go", kab'e "go!" |

Epenthetic i: the written standard inserts i between n-/xt-/t- and a consonant-initial stem (niwär, xtib'e, tib'e), and between xt-/t- and the plural Set A markers qa-/ki- (xtiqab'än, tiqab'ana', tikitzu'). Before a bare stem the i is sometimes left unwritten (nwär beside niwär), but after xt- and t- it is not optional before qa- and ki-: write xtiqab'än, never *xtqab'än (Chapter 13).

| 3p | nkitz'ët | xkitz'ët | xtikitz'ët | tikitz'eta' |

| 2s | nakanoj | xakanoj | xtakanoj | takanoj |

| 3p | nkikanoj | xkikanoj | xtikikanoj | tikikanoj |

| Subject | Incompletive | Completive | Potential | Imperative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1s | ninya' | xinya' | xtinya' | tinya' |
| 2s | naya' | xaya' | xtaya' | taya' |
| 3s | nuya' | xuya' | xtuya' | tuya' |
| 1p | nqaya' | xqaya' | xtiqaya' | tiqaya' |
| 2p | niya' | xiya' | xtiya' | tiya' |
| 3p | nkiya' | xkiya' | xtikiya' | tikiya' |

**Vowel-initial stems** take the prevocalic Set A: ninwajo', nawajo', nrajo', nqajo', niwajo', nkajo' "I want it, you want it..."; completive xinwajo', xawajo', xrajo', xqajo', xiwajo', xkajo'.

**Imperative vowel harmony (root transitives).** ä > a' (tab'ana' "do it"), e/ë/i/ï > a' (tatz'eta' "look at it", tatija' "eat it", tawila' "find it"), o/ö > o' (taloq'o' "buy it", tamolo' "gather it"), u/ü > u' (tak'utu' "show it", tachupu' "put it out"). Glottal-final roots add nothing (taya', tatzu', tato', tasu').

### A.5 Subject and object combined: -tz'ët in the incompletive

Rows give the subject (Set A), columns the object (Set B). Cells where subject and object are the same person use the reflexive -i' instead (nintz'ët wi' "I see myself").

| Subject \ Object | me | you | him/her/it | us | you (pl) | them |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I | (nintz'ët wi') | yatintz'ët | nintz'ët | | yixintz'ët | ye'intz'ët |
| you | yinatz'ët | (natz'ët awi') | natz'ët | yojatz'ët | | ye'atz'ët |
| he/she | yirutz'ët | yarutz'ët | nutz'ët | yojrutz'ët | yixrutz'ët | yerutz'ët |
| we | | yaqatz'ët | nqatz'ët | (nqatz'ët qi') | yixqatz'ët | yeqatz'ët |
| you (pl) | yinitz'ët | | nitz'ët | yojitz'ët | (nitz'ët iwi') | ye'itz'ët |
| they | yikitz'ët | yakitz'ët | nkitz'ët | yojkitz'ët | yixkitz'ët | yekitz'ët |

In the completive replace y- with x- and n- with x- (xatintz'ët "I saw you", xutz'ët "he saw it", xe'intz'ët "I saw them"); in the potential use xk-/xt- (xkatintz'ët, xtutz'ët); in the imperative use k-/t- (kinatz'eta' "look at me", ke'atz'eta' "look at them", kojato' "help us").

### A.6 Voice and the perfect

| Verb | Transitive (3s did it) | Passive (it was done) | Antipassive (he did, agent focus) | Perfect (he has done it) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| -b'än do | xub'än | xb'an | xb'anon | rub'anon |
| -löq' buy | xulöq' | xloq' | xloq'on | ruloq'on |
| -tz'ët see | xutz'ët | xtz'et (also xtz'etëx) | xtz'eton | rutz'eton |
| -chäp grab | xuchäp | xchap (also xchapäx) | xchapon | ruchapon |
| -k'äm take | xuk'äm | xk'am | xk'amon | ruk'amon |
| -tij eat | xutij | xtij | xtijon | rutijon |
| -ya' give | xuya' | xya' | xya'on | ruya'on |
| -to' help | xuto' | xto' | xto'on | ruto'on |
| -k'utuj ask | xuk'utuj | xk'utüx | xk'utun | ruk'utun |
| -tz'ib'aj write | xutz'ib'aj | xtz'ib'äx | xtz'ib'an | rutz'ib'an |
| -q'etej hug | xuq'etej | xq'etëx | xq'eten | ruq'eten |
| -kanoj look for | xukanoj | xkanöx | xkanon | rukanon |
| -etamaj learn | xretamaj | xetamäx | xetaman | retaman "he knows" |

Rules: root transitives tense the vowel for the passive (xub'än > xb'an) and add -on for the antipassive and perfect; derived -Vj verbs take -Vx with a lax vowel for the passive and -Vn for the antipassive and perfect. The agent of a passive is introduced with roma/-oma; the patient of an antipassive with richin/-ichin. The perfect carries Set A and no aspect prefix; its intransitive counterpart is -inäq/-näq: b'enäq "gone", petenäq "come", kosinäq (kosnäq) "tired", kaminäq "dead", sachinäq "lost", nojnäq "full", alaxnäq "born", etz'aninäq "having played", ik'owinäq "passed".

Roots ending in l or r take -an instead of a lax vowel + l for the stative (xulan, b'olan, tzalan, tz'iran "deserted"). Subjects of statives are the free Set B words: in tz'uyül, at pa'äl, öj kotz'öl, e jotöl.

| Relational noun | 1s | 2s | 3s | 1p | 2p | 3p | Core meaning |

| -ichin | wichin | awichin | richin | qichin | iwichin | kichin | of, belonging to; for; patient of antipassive |
| -oma (-uma) | woma | awoma | roma | qoma | iwoma | koma | because of; agent of passive |
| -ik'in (-uk'in) | wik'in | awik'in | rik'in | qik'in | iwik'in | kik'in | with; at the house of |
| chi + -e | chwe | chawe | chre (chi re) | chqe | chiwe | chike (chke) | to, for (recipient) |
| chi + -wäch | chi nuwäch | chawäch (chi awäch) | chuwäch (chwäch) | chi qawäch | chi iwäch | chi kiwäch | in front of; to the face of; compared with |
| chi + -ij | chwij | chawij | chrij (chi rij) | chi qij | chi iwij | chi kij | behind; about; after |
| chi + -xe' | chi nuxe' | chaxe' | chuxe' (chi ruxe') | chi qaxe' | chi ixe' | chi kixe' | under |
| pa + -wi' | pa nuwi' | pa awi' | pa ruwi' | pa qawi' | pan iwi' | pa kiwi' | on top of; above; about |
| chi / pa + -pam | pa nupam | pa apam | chupam (pa rupam) | pa qapam | pan ipam | pa kipam | inside |
| chi + -kojol | | | chukojol (chi rukojol) | chi qakojol | chi ikojol | chi kikojol | between, among |
| xe + -xikin | xe nuxikin | xe axikin | xe ruxikin (xe ruxkin, chi ruxikin) | xe qaxikin | xe ixikin | xe kixikin | beside, next to |
| chi + -chi' | chi nuchi' | chi achi' | chuchi' | chi qachi' | chi ichi' | chi kichi' | at the edge of, at the mouth of |
| -i' | wi' | awi' | ri' | qi' | iwi' | ki' | myself, yourself...; each other |
| -yon | nuyon | ayon | ruyon | qayon | iyon | kiyon | alone, by oneself |
| -onojel | | | ronojel (all of it) | qonojel | iwonojel | konojel | all (of us/you/them) |

When does chi fuse with what follows? Whenever the possessive prefix is a bare consonant or begins with a vowel, so that preposition and prefix make one easy syllable: chi + w- > chw- (chwe, chwij), chi + aw- > chaw- (chawe, chawäch), chi + r- > chr- (chre, chrij), chi + q- > chq- (chqe), and chi + ru- > chu- with the r dropped (chuwäch, chuxe', chupam, chuchi', chukojol). Before the full syllables nu-, qa-, i- and ki- it stays a separate word: chi nuwäch, chi qawäch, chi iwäch, chi kiwäch. The fusable forms also circulate written apart (chi re, chi rij, chi ruxe'); both spellings are correct, so be consistent within a text (Chapter 22).

**Ordinals:** nab'ey first, ruka'n second, rox third, rukaj fourth, ro' fifth, ruwaq sixth, ruwuq seventh, ruwaqxaq eighth, rub'elej ninth, rulaj tenth, rujulaj eleventh; k'isib'äl last.

**Distributives:** jujun one by one (also "each, some"), kaka' two by two, ox'öx by threes, kajkäj by fours, wotäq by fives, waqtäq by sixes, wuqtäq, waqxaqtäq, b'elejtäq, lajtäq.

**Times:** jumul once, kamul twice, oxmul three times; ¿jampe mul? how many times?

## Glossary of grammatical terms

**Absolutive (Set B).** The pronoun set that marks the subject of an intransitive verb, the object of a transitive verb, and the subject of a non-verbal predicate. Forms: i-/in-, a-/at-, Ø, oj-, ix-, e-/e'- on verbs; in, at, Ø, öj, ïx, e as free words.

**Agent.** The participant that performs an action. In a transitive verb the agent is marked by Set A; in a passive it is optionally expressed with roma; in an antipassive it is the Set B subject.

**Agentive suffix.** -el (plural -ela') making "one who does": tijonel "teacher", samajel "worker", k'ayinel "vendor".

**Animacy hierarchy.** The ranking (people > animals > plants and things) that governs whether a noun takes a plural suffix: high-animacy nouns take -a'/-i', low-animacy nouns stay unmarked or take taq.

**Antipassive.** A voice that makes a transitive verb intransitive by demoting the object; the agent becomes the Set B subject. Root transitives add -on, derived transitives replace -Vj with -Vn. Required when the agent is questioned or relativized.

**Aspect.** The grammatical category that says how an event relates to time: ongoing (incompletive), finished (completive), expected or possible (potential). Kaqchikel marks aspect rather than tense; the English past, present and future are approximations.

**Causative.** A transitive verb meaning "cause to X", derived from an intransitive with -isaj: -wär "sleep" > -wartisaj "put to sleep".

**Chiasmus.** A rhetorical figure in which a second phrase reverses the order of elements of the first (A B, B A); common in formal Kaqchikel.

**Completive.** The aspect of completed events, marked by x-. Usually translated by the English past.

**Couplet.** Two parallel words or phrases that together name one idea: qate' qatata' "our ancestors", ruwäch ulew "the world".

**Deictic.** A pointing word: re...re' "this", la...la' "that", ri...ri' "that (known)", wawe' "here", chi ri' "there".

**Derived transitive.** A transitive verb stem ending in -Vj (-kanoj, -k'utuj, -tz'ib'aj). Takes no suffix in the imperative; passive in -Vx, antipassive in -Vn.

**Directional.** An uninflected particle after the verb that adds direction or permanence: pe "toward here", el "away", apo "toward there", kan "remaining", qa "down", aqanäj "up".

**Epenthetic vowel.** A vowel inserted to ease pronunciation, like the i in niwär or xtib'e; often written, sometimes not.

**Ergative (Set A).** The pronoun set that marks the subject of a transitive verb and the possessor of a noun. Forms on verbs: in-/inw-, a-/aw-, ru-/r-, qa-/q-, i-/iw-, ki-/k-; on nouns the first person singular is nu-/w- (nupo't, wochoch), the rest are the same.

**Focus.** Putting a phrase first in the sentence (often with ja) to single it out: ja ri umül xb'anon "it was the rabbit who did it".

**Glottal stop.** The catch in the throat written with the apostrophe ('); a full consonant in Kaqchikel, not written at the start of a word.

**Glottalized consonant.** A consonant made with a closed glottis: b', ch', k', q', t', tz'.

**Hortative.** The mood of commands, wishes and "let's": prefix t- before zero 3sB, k- elsewhere. Used for first and third person as well as second.

**Imperative.** The second person command form, a subtype of the hortative: kab'e "go!", tab'ana' "do it!".

**Incompletive.** The aspect of ongoing, habitual or scheduled events, marked by n- before zero 3sB and y- elsewhere. Usually translated by the English present.

**Intransitive verb.** A verb with one participant (its subject), marked by Set B: yib'e "I go".

**Irrealis.** The particle ta marking something not real: the second half of negation (man ... ta), wishes (ninwajo' ta), conditions (manta ... ta).

**Lax vowel.** One of the short, centralized vowels ä, ë, ï, ö, ü, found only in the last syllable of a word; they become tense when a suffix is added.

**Morpheme.** The smallest meaningful piece of a word: in xutij, the morphemes are x-, Ø, u-, -tij.

**Non-verbal predicate.** A predicate that is not a verb (a noun, adjective, positional stative or k'o); its subject is a free Set B word: in tijonel, at ütz, e tz'uyül, öj k'o.

**Passive.** A voice that makes a transitive verb intransitive by promoting the object to subject; root transitives tense the vowel (xub'än > xb'an), derived transitives take -Vx (xuk'utuj > xk'utüx).

**Patient.** The participant that undergoes the action; the object of a transitive verb, the subject of a passive, an oblique richin-phrase in an antipassive.

**Perfect.** The form Set A + stem + -on (root) or -Vn (derived) with no aspect prefix, meaning "has done": rub'anon "he has done it", wetaman "I know". Intransitive perfects end in -inäq/-näq: b'enäq "gone".

**Positional.** A CVC root naming a position or state (tz'uy- "seated") that derives a stative (tz'uyül), an intransitive (-tz'uye'), a transitive (-tz'uyub'a') and adjectives (tz'uyutz'ik).

**Possessive prefix.** Set A on a noun: nutz'i' "my dog", wochoch "my house".

**Potential.** The aspect of future or possible events, marked by xt- before zero 3sB and xk- elsewhere.

**Predicate.** The part of the sentence that says something about the subject; in Kaqchikel it comes first.

**Prefix / suffix.** A morpheme attached before / after a stem.

**Reduplication.** Repeating a word or part of it for intensity or distribution: ütz ütz "very good", q'ij q'ij "every day", ojer ojer kan.

**Relational noun.** A possessed noun that does the work of an English preposition or conjunction: wichin "mine", roma "because of him", chuwäch "in front of it".

**Root transitive.** A one-syllable CVC transitive verb with a lax vowel (-b'än, -tz'ët, -löq'); takes -V' in the imperative, tenses its vowel in the passive.

**Set A / Set B.** See ergative / absolutive.

**Stative.** A positional form in -Vl or -an (tz'uyül, pa'äl, xulan) describing a position already reached; takes free Set B subjects.

**Stem.** The part of the verb to which aspect and pronoun prefixes attach; may be a bare root or a derived form.

**Tense vowel.** One of the full vowels a, e, i, o, u, as opposed to the lax ä, ë, ï, ö, ü.

**Transitive verb.** A verb with two participants, the subject (Set A) and the object (Set B): nintz'ët "I see it", yatintz'ët "I see you".

**Versive.** An intransitive verb of becoming in -är/-ir: -nimär "get big", -tewär "get cold".

**Vowel harmony.** The imperative suffix of root transitives copying the root vowel: taloq'o', tak'utu', tab'ana'.

**VOS.** The basic order verb, object, subject: xutij ri kinäq' ri umül "the rabbit ate the beans"; SVO is now also common.
